_README: This file is NOT read by Vercel. It is the block to paste into the MAIN
project's vercel.json, which lives one directory up at gs-fe-content/vercel.json
(groovesheet-fe's root). Paste it and redeploy the main project.
WHY: the content app is its own Vercel project on its own domain. These
rewrites put its four route trees on www.groovesheet.net, so the blog earns
authority for the main domain rather than for a Vercel subdomain, and the
portal is reachable at the address people expect.
ORDER MATTERS, in two places, and both are easy to get wrong:
1. `/api/internal/:path*` MUST come BEFORE the existing `/api/:path*` entry.
Vercel takes the first rewrite that matches. `/api/:path*` sends
everything to api.groovesheet.net, so if it goes first every portal
action (sign in, save, approve, send) 404s against the Python backend,
which has no such routes.
2. The two `redirects` entries whose source is
`/:path((?!api/|zh-CN|zh-TW|static/|.*\.).*)` send visitors in China to
the Chinese locale. They match /blog and /internal too. Left alone, a
reader in China lands on /zh-CN/blog, which the CRA app renders from the
OLD blog_posts reader and which therefore shows none of the posts this
pipeline publishes. Add blog, blog-media and internal to the negative
lookahead in BOTH redirect sources, as shown under _redirectSourceFix
below. The blog is English-only for now (see pipeline.config.json), so
a Chinese visitor should reach the same English post as everyone else,
not a locale that has nothing behind it.
Replace CONTENT_APP_URL below with the content project's production URL.
Vercel needs the protocol: https://groovesheet-content.vercel.app, or a
custom domain if one is set. Do not point it at the git-branch URL, which
changes on every deploy.

_redirectSourceFix.note: Apply to BOTH redirect entries that use this source. There are two: one for the CN geo rule on the bare path and one for the cookie-missing case.

_rewritesToAdd._note: The app's JS and CSS. next.config.mjs sets assetPrefix to /content-assets. Without this every page arrives as bare HTML: the CRA catch-all answers /_next/* and /content-assets/* with index.html and a 200, so nothing hydrates and /internal/login cannot sign in. Do not rewrite /_next/* instead; the main app will own that path once it is Next.js.

The blog's own sitemap. The site-wide /sitemap.xml stays pointed at api.groovesheet.net; this is a second sitemap, and both get submitted in Search Console. See src/app/sitemap.ts for why there are two.

/api/cron/content: Deliberately absent. Vercel Cron calls the cron path on the project that
declares it, which is the content project itself (see its vercel.json).
It never goes through the main domain, and exposing it there would add a
public door to a job that only CRON_SECRET protects.

_afterwards: Once the main project is redeployed, check all four on the real domain:
curl -sI https://www.groovesheet.net/internal/login, then fetch one /content-assets/_next/static/... src from its HTML: expect application/javascript, not text/html
The second one is the important one: it is an existing indexed URL that
must not break on the day this ships.
